描述_ZN: Ink Brush Landscape" scroll, modern, painted by Chen Shizeng, on silk with ink brush, 67 cm in length and 27.3 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "The mountain air is pale and the spring is squeaking. Zhongnian Xianya appreciates it. In the sixth month of the year Cincun, Hengyan." Inscriptions: "Seal of Heng Ke" and "Seal of the decaying man".　　The "chen" in the self-title is the fifth year of the Republic of China (1916).　　The picture depicts a high mountain range, a waterfall with flowing clouds, and a secluded house in a lush forest.　　This landscape painting, made in 1916, is one of the earlier works in Chen Shizeng's painting. The composition of the work is robust, the brushwork is deep, and the repeated chaffing and dabbing are very different from his later method of painting landscapes without chaffing, which obviously carries the meaning of Gong Xian's brushwork and ink, the first of the "Eight Artists of Jinling". Chen Shizeng began to paint landscapes directly from the ancients, especially from painters of the opposite school of painting to the Four Kings, Gong Xian being one of them. In learning to use the painting methods of the ancients, Chen Shizeng adopted the attitude of taking the ancients for his own use without being subservient to them, and integrated the brushwork of the ancients so that he could paint with ease.
